why: Sleep and pain can influence one another. Looking for patterns is more useful than blaming yourself for an imperfect night.

slides.title: A Two-Way Relationship
slides.content: Pain can disrupt sleep, and poor sleep can affect pain sensitivity, energy, mood, and concentration the next day.

slides.title: Needs Vary
slides.content: Many adults are advised to get at least seven hours regularly, but individual needs and circumstances differ.

slides.title: More Than Duration
slides.content: Timing, regularity, continuity, and how rested you feel can all matter. One number does not tell the whole story.

slides.title: Avoid the Perfect-Sleep Trap
slides.content: One difficult night does not erase recovery. Focus on patterns and realistic changes you can sustain.

slides.title: Try One Experiment
slides.content: Choose one change—such as a consistent wake time, a wind-down period, or a more comfortable sleep setup—and notice the response.
